![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14129388/assets/ff6c3e308d89c9d07cff993f097fe2fcfafb22dab3399b9056f8db167b1b4b80.png)

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the curves $y=2x$ and $y={x}^{2}$ in the first quadrant, as shown above. If the mass density function of $D$ is given by $\lambda (x,y)=6x+14y,$ find the moment of inertia of the lamina about the $y$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 2x\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14129388/assets/fb20e4c3052e28aeb2e6dad5054b0458db2d3b23d10991cfae27b5b00655a8fe.png)

Using the formula for ${I}_{y},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2x}{x}^{2}(6x+14y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2x}6{x}^{3}+14{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[6{x}^{3}y+7{x}^{2}{y}^{2}]_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(12{x}^{4}+28{x}^{4})-(6{x}^{5}+7{x}^{6})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}40{x}^{4}-6{x}^{5}-7{x}^{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[8{x}^{5}-{x}^{6}-{x}^{7}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =256-64-128 \\  & =64.\end{aligned}
$$
